title: Forces: artifacts through consequence
scope: Design proposal grounded in current source inspection; no museum/runtime/manuscript/order changes, no new Godot tests.
principle: One familiar point acquires abilities. Each encounter starts with an ordinary task; added relations produce consequences the task did not specify.
route_note: Keep the earlier proposed ability progression: push → launch → two-hand flight → release/brake → vortex → deflect → tethered return → combination. This proposal does not promote that order into the canonical thirteen-hall spine. The mobile is optional; the reluctant plinth returns after spring force rather than smuggling springs into the first motion lesson.
kit: The familiar black PointBody and explicit receiver behavior
A plain off-white movable plinth or trolley
A tether with an explicit fixed or dynamic anchor
A bounded field source and declared affected bodies
A few loose blocks plus an inspectable reset
tests_overview: Verify mechanisms independently, then their interaction. Keep one baseline success possible. Preserve state between action and aftermath. Test local laws and reset without prescribing an emergent outcome.

cards.title: The point that can carry you
cards.goal: Push the familiar sphere; later use two instances to reach a ledge yourself.
cards.learn: Finite push → retained velocity → two contributions to thrust. Teach these in successive encounters.
cards.turn: One hand lets go while the other still thrusts. You continue drifting; the remaining contribution changes the journey rather than cancelling it.
cards.agency: Release, counter-thrust or use the landing court; camera orientation remains level.
cards.status: Existing point lineage and field receiver adapter; two-sphere flight remains proposed. The current catalyst auto-returns after a drop, which needs a deliberate policy for the force continuation.
cards.check: One movement owner sums contributions; release removes only that hand's thrust. Accepted control stays aim down/back + triggers → thrust up/forward. Firing is a separate action or explicit mode.

cards.title: The launch pad and the landing tray
cards.goal: Send the point to a nearby tray, then make the crossing yourself.
cards.learn: Launch state, gravity and contact at landing. Distinguish setting velocity from applying an impulse.
cards.turn: A successful landing strikes a loose tray, which slides into another body. Arrival becomes the start of a second event.
cards.agency: Adjust launch direction, restrain the tray or change the landing surface.
cards.status: Installed launch pad exists; a movable receiving tray and freely interacting landing encounter are new.
cards.check: One launch per entry; retain post-launch motion. A floor sensor applies its declared rule to allowed body types, not only a theatrical player trigger.

cards.title: The reluctant plinth
cards.goal: Move the point on a small trolley to its display plinth.
cards.learn: Begin with contact and friction. Return after spring force is introduced to add an elastic pull.
cards.turn: The wheel catches; pulling stores energy. When it comes free the trolley reaches a second object before the player has caught up with the consequence.
cards.agency: Change route, reduce the pull, move the obstruction or brake. A quiet successful delivery must also be possible.
cards.status: These are reference studies, not a reusable interacting trolley. Friction ramp integrates a prescribed lane, spring tower uses a one-axis solver, collision carts display ideal outcomes. A coupled room-scale receiver must be built.
cards.check: The held tether stores energy; removing the pull does not erase motion. No collision animation determines the ending. First test one catch and one free run before adding loose blocks.

cards.title: The retrieving point
cards.goal: Bring a loose sphere back to your hand using the held catalyst.
cards.learn: A position-dependent attraction acts on declared receivers; the source does not understand the player's preferred target.
cards.turn: The field also pulls a doorstop or movable support. The requested sphere comes closer while something else changes the passage.
cards.agency: Move the source, shorten the radius, use a target filter or release attraction and watch the remaining motion.
cards.status: The existing held point already queries nearby rigid bodies and applies bounded central forces. Consistent receiver props and the doorstop encounter are proposed.
cards.check: Test the mask/filter explicitly; separate source position from target intention. Release removes attraction, not the receiver's accumulated velocity. Keep the inverse-distance term finite near the source.

cards.title: The collecting room
cards.goal: Gather scattered spheres into a shallow central basin; later enter the field yourself.
cards.learn: Radial and tangential field contributions act on existing velocity. Change one term at a time.
cards.turn: Gathering becomes orbiting or crowding. The same rule catches loose supports as well as the intended collection; entry speed changes the result.
cards.agency: Alter the field, move its centre or counter-thrust through it. The field is not guaranteed to tidy the room.
cards.status: The installed vortex replaces player velocity. This continuation requires a force/acceleration contribution that preserves incoming motion; it is a new variant, not an already available emergent field.
cards.check: Entry/exit do not clear velocity; centre remains finite; receiver rules are explicit. Begin with loose points before adding the player.

cards.title: The point that insists on returning
cards.goal: Deflect a tethered sphere to open a passage.
cards.learn: Restoring force, damping and a visible anchor. Reuse the same target body from the shooting study.
cards.turn: The point swings back. In a later version the anchor sits on a movable plinth, so the place it returns to also moves.
cards.agency: Time a crossing, move the anchor, damp the return or wedge the target aside. Destruction need not be the only solution.
cards.status: A clear one-axis spring study and form-firing catalyst exist. A free spatial tether, movable anchor and true impulse target require new receiver work.
cards.check: Compare fixed and movable anchors explicitly. Equal-and-opposite spring response when both ends are dynamic; no double-counted shot impulse. Opponent variants: free point, tethered point, then optional bounded pursuing point.

cards.title: The body you keep adding to
cards.goal: Hang the point so that it rests level; add one familiar object.
cards.learn: Support, torque and mass distribution. Add a rigid wind-catching plate only after the balance is legible.
cards.turn: The addition shifts the balance. A powered fan then acts on the added plate and sets the rest moving; the body now responds differently because of what it carries.
cards.agency: Move an attachment, add a counterweight or keep an asymmetry. No perfect balance is required for the object to be worth keeping.
cards.status: Existing mobile references provide a visual vocabulary. The inspected prop_mobile freezes its nested rigid bodies and arranges balance; a freely joined kinetic assemblage would be a new physical variant. Other mobile implementations need separate inspection.
cards.check: Attachments must actually participate in mass/inertia and constraints. State the fan's force model. Begin with rigid parts; cloth and soft-body simulation can wait.

cards.title: The delivery room
cards.role: Final combination / no new compulsory law
cards.goal: Carry one point across a room using the abilities and tools already learned.
cards.learn: Composition and observation: launch, brake, gather, redirect and return remain the same operations.
cards.turn: An automated conveyor keeps delivering props while the receiver slows. Moving one jam changes what meets the next body. A blockage may become a support or just remain a blockage.
cards.agency: Stop a feed, take another route, retrieve the point or preserve an interesting arrangement. A manual reset starts a new experiment; it should not silently erase the aftermath.
cards.status: Existing conveyor_backlog uses actual rigid boxes, a moving-surface collider, a timed receiver and a finite pool. A complete carrying task combining the selected artifacts remains a proposal.
cards.check: Reuse the learned rules; bound the number of bodies visibly. Validate restart and retained state. Do not demand a particular collapse or funny ending as the success criterion.
